newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan leader invited to international conference.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan leader invited to international conference.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui has been invited to Panama in September 1997 for an international conference at which Lee may meet the leaders of the United States and France, state-funded television reported on Saturday.
The move is sure to anger China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949 and tried to prevent Taiwanese leaders from attending international forums.

Panama, one of Taiwan's only 30 diplomatic allies, has decided to invite Lee for the international canal conference and a Panamanian representative is scheduled to arrive in Taiwan on Sunday with the invitation, the television said.
"The key participants of the conference are Panama, the United States and France," Taiwan's ambassador to Panama, Yuan Chien-sheng, said in a telephone interview with the television.
"We are a very big client of its canal, so the Republic of China is very important for Panama," Yuan said from Panama, noting close economic ties between the two sides.
"If President Lee attends the conference, he is expected to meet many leaders including U.S. President Bill Clinton and French President Jacques Chirac at the conference," the television said.
Washington and Paris recognise Beijing, not Taipei.

Taiwan's latest bid to send its leaders to international forums failed after Philippine President Fidel Ramos declined to invite Lee to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum summit to be held in Manila in November.
Both Taiwan and China say they want reunification, but under very different terms.
China says Taiwan is not entitled to foreign ties while Taiwan insists that its 21 million people have the right to take part in international activities.
Lee's private but high-profile visit to the United States in June 1995 infuriated China and sent bilateral ties to their lowest level since the late 1980s, when political tensions started to thaw.
Panama will also invite Chang Yung-fa, chairman of Taiwan's shipping giant Evergreen Group, to the conference, the television said.
Evergreen, a major foreign investor in Panama, plans to spend up to US$200 million on a new port facility being built on Panama's Atlantic coast and is applying to set up an airline there.
The Taiwan government also publicly encourages its businessmen to invest in Panama.
